title.narrative: Upscaling the Capacity-building programme for the nomination of World Heritage sites in the Africa Region: Second phase

description.narrative: The project addresses Africa’s underrepresentation on the UNESCO World Heritage List by tackling its root causes, limited technical expertise and experts, fragile institutions, and under-resourced heritage sectors. It will support nomination processes and reinforce international cooperation by strengthening national capacities, training young experts and enhance exchanges of knowledge. Building upon the successful first phase (2021-2025), this second phase will consolidate progress, upscale impact and ensure long-term sustainability of the first phase. First, this will be achieved through deepened support to the remaining seven States Parties with no properties inscribed and no nomination proposals under examination. Comoros and São Tomé and Principe having already submitted nomination dossiers, which will be examined in 2026, Burundi, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eswatini, Liberia, Somalia, and South Sudan will be supported to develop and/or advance their nomination proposals for World Heritage. The project will then enhance continental expertise by empowering all African States Parties to engage with the new and mandatory Preliminary Assessment process, while offering targeted support to Small Island Developing States. It will also foster sustained knowledge exchange through the mentorship programme and workshops with Japanese experts, ensuring that African practitioners are equipped to lead long-term, sustainable heritage practices.
